I. What is meant by accommodation of the human eye?
II. What is the near point of a normal eye and what does it signify?

OR

I. What is dispersion of light?
II. Which colour of light deviates the least during dispersion through a

different colours while passing through a glass prism.

[CBSE Class X Science, marking scheme, 2026-27]
39. Students to attempt either option A or B. 5
A.
I. Accommodation: Ability of the eye lens to change its focal length to
focus objects at different distances on the retina. (1)
II. Near point: The nearest point (about 25 cm for a normal eye) at
which an object can be seen distinctly; it signifies the closest
comfortable focus. (1)
III. Lens for defect (cannot see distant objects): A diverging (concave)
lens is used to correct myopia (short-sightedness). (1)
IV. Diagram:
(2)
B.
I. Dispersion: Splitting of white light into its component colours due to
wavelength-dependent refraction. (1)
II. Colour deviating least in prism: Red deviates least (longest
wavelength). (1)
